entry.title: How to redshirt in College Football 26
entry.summary:
Athletes in College Football 26's Dynasty mode have a limited number of years they can play for your school, and you can redshirt to keep some of them around for a longer time.
Having good squad depth is necessary, as some of your roster members can get injured and miss a chunk of a season. However, you can sometimes have just too many talents wasting time on your bench. You can then redshirt some of them to save a year, so let's get started.
College Football 26 redshirt guide
When you redshirt an athlete, they will earn an additional collegiate year. This is perfect for someone who can't join your squad outright. However, they might still be a late developer, or just someone you believe in. The additional Freshman year not only allows them extra game time, but they will also get more experience during that additional year.
Start your Dynasty mode save.
Use the R1 button to scroll right, and do so until you reach the Team tab.
Scroll down to the second last option, which says Redshirts.
This area will show you your full roster while highlighting athletes who are eligible to apply for the redshirt status. This is key: not every athlete can have the status.
Select a valid athlete, then press the X/A to apply the redshirt status.
Screenshot by Destructoid
There are specific limitations to this status.
Redshirt status can be applied only once in an athlete's career.
You can play a redshirt up to four games during their Freshman year. More appearance will automatically discard their status.
There's a transfer portal in Dynasty mode, and one or more of your redshirted athletes could use it to transfer to another school. This could happen when you can't match their game time expectations.
You can also apply the redshirt status in Road to Glory, but in that case, it's not entirely dependent on you. In Road to Glory, the choice to apply redshirt on yourself will also depend on your coach and coordinators.

Video games are a wonderful medium, if only for the sole fact that you have a direct impact on what's going on within them, unlike movies or books.

Some games, however, have the opposite effect. The last thing I need sometimes after a long or frustrating day is to hop onto Marvel Rivals and get tilted at bad teammates or toxic comms.
That's why there are such things as comfort games, or even games that we play to boost our mood when we need it most. It could be anything from a classic singleplayer adventure, the current hot AAA title, a cozy indie game, or just about anything with a group of friends or loved ones to keep your mind off everyday ills.
For me, when my mood is in the pits, I gravitate to singleplayer titles. For the most part, they don't frustrate me like another human being in a multiplayer game can, so I like to lose myself in the world of recent games like Donkey Kong Bananza, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, or a cozy titledevoid of any need for effort, something like Unpacking.
And so now, I ask you, dear reader, what is the kind of game you turn to when you need to turn your mood around? Let us know in the poll and comments below, and maybe offer some suggestions for those who may be looking to try out something new in the world of positive thoughts and vibes.

entry.title: This upcoming Steam game is literally just Cult of the Lamb but with dinosaurs, and I’m suddenly very hyped
entry.summary:
Just about every day, I receive emails about upcoming Steam indies and new demos, and I download them for a time when I can get around to playing them.
Earlier this week I got an email about a demo for a game called Dino Topia, so I downloaded it, and just got around to trying it out for the first time. I'm happy to report that it's legitimately Cult of the Lamb, but with dinosaurs, and it's awesome.
Image via Celestial Studio
For those who missed out on the Cult of the Lamb hype, the cute, base-building roguelike was a massive hit when it launched in August 2022 from Devolver Digital and Massive Monster, and it's one of the more satisfying and fun casual games in recent years.
Dino Topia has the same exact formula—build a base to farm materials and house your residents, who are dinosaurs, and go out on roguelike expeditions to advance the story, recruit new dinos, and get more materials.
This game swaps the lamb for a caveperson, and swaps the cute animals for cute dinosaurs, and the gameplay allows you to bring up to three dinos with you on your adventure as you fight your way through dungeons to find new dinos and more.
Cult of the Lamb (and from what I've played, Dino Topia too) scratches a really niche itch when it comes to building your base, breeding allies, populating your base with them and putting them to work, and supplementing it all with exploratory combat in changing environments with randomized power-ups to pick up along the way. It seems like a solid investment for Cult of the Lamb fans when it drops next month.
Screenshot by Destructoid
The Dino Topia demo is available now, and you can wishlist the full title ahead of its August release date now.

entry.title: Come slide with me through loopy shooter maps in this homage to Counter-Strike's beloved glitch surfing
entry.summary:
Counter-Strike surfing is a modded game mode for Valve's bomb defusal FPS in which players skate through obstacle courses by means of a physics glitch. It has a proud history dating back to 2004, when modder Charles "Mariowned" Joyce discovered that it was far more enjoyable to slide off roofs than shoot people in his custom map Killbox. So he made a new map dedicated to sliding, The Gap. Thus the greasy chute that led to Alice0 (RPS in peace) hailing CS surfing as "the esport we deserve" in 2020.
People have crafted their own versions of the mode in games like Roblox, and Proper Game Developers such as Blizzard have seemingly taken inspiration - Overwatch's Lucio is surely a love letter to the mode. Now here comes SurfsUp, a free-to-play surfing game in the Godot Engine. Released this month, it's been favourably compared to surf maps in Valve's Counter-Strike 2, and is worth a pop even if you have no prior experience of counters or striking. entry.title: Shark Dentist is about operating on a fool's idea of a shark
entry.summary: Former RPS sealife correspondent Nate once described the game Maneater as "an ecstatically violent simulation of being a fool's idea of a shark", which stuck with me. The Jaws Effect is a reasonably well known phenomenon coined in a paper that explores the impact the 1975 film had on Australian policy response to shark bites, although the term is now used a bit more broadly to refer to how sharks are villainised in pop culture - villainisation obviously being an absurdly human and dramatic concept to apply to a hungry or scared fish. Jaws did actually result in an increase in shark culls, but its lasting legacy has also been argued to be more insididous. Depending on whether you're looking at stats from the UN or from conservation charities, the number of sharks killed or mutilated and harvested each year for fins and other parts ranges between about 10 and 100 million, and it's been argued this continues with relatively little pushback as compared to similar wildlife atrocities due to wide-reaching perception that ranges from apathy to vilification. A sharknado of lies, if you will. Read more

To help us during the testing period, dig out your Nature & Sciences CD, grab a daily build and read our testing guidelines. You will also need an existing installation from the base Adibou 2: Environment CD, and to copy the contents of your Nature & Sciences CD into a freely named subdirectory of the main game directory, as described in our wiki. Then, register the expansion in-game via the "Land of Knowledge" screen, and start collecting sweets as you complete Adibou's activities…or encourage a young relative to do so!
